# [南科聚焦 News ![Image 6](https://www.sustech.edu.cn/static/newest2-v4/img/icon/News.png)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/ [link_13])[南科大新闻网![Image 7](https://www.sustech.edu.cn/static/newest2-v4/img/jiantou/6.png)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/ [link_13])

![Image 8](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/full/2026/10/011790822150772209.jpg)### [南方科技大学举行升旗仪式 庆祝中华人民共和国成立77周年](link_115)

![Image 9](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/full/2026/08/221787368555120419.png)### [Nature | 南科大徐俊课题组合作揭示GPCR通过二聚/寡聚化重塑细胞信号通路改善药理活性的分子基础](link_116)

*   [![Image 10](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/large/2026/09/171789637358501217.jpg)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/html/202609/47893.html [link_117])
#### [南方科技大学以正确政绩观凝心铸魂 以实干担当推动高质量发展](link_117)

中央部署开展树立和践行正确政绩观学习教育以来，南方科技大学党委坚持以习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想为指导，深入学习贯彻习近平总书记重要讲话和重要指示批示精神，认真贯彻中央和省委、市委、市委教育工委相关工作要求，紧扣“立党为公、为民造福、科学决策、真抓实干”总要求，把学习教育作为全年工作的重中之重，一体推进学习研讨、查摆问题、整改整治、建章立制、开门教育，以学促干、以干践行，坚持通过锤炼党性确保党员干部树立和践行正确政绩观，在学思践悟中筑牢思想根基，在实干担当中践行初心使命。 2026-09-17[![Image 11](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/large/2026/09/201789888983895632.png)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/html/202609/47904.html [link_118])
#### [南方科技大学“鹏城南科一号”卫星成功入轨 “硬核”创新再结硕果](link_118)

9月20日12时03分，南方科技大学“鹏城南科一号（PEGA－SUS 1）” 暨鹏城首发卫星，由我国商业运载火箭力箭一号遥十八在酒泉卫星发射基地成功发射，顺利进入预定轨道。中国科学院院士、南方科技大学校长薛其坤与师生代表共同观礼卫星发射。 2026-09-20[![Image 12](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/large/2026/09/11102509_91181.png)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/html/202609/47875.html [link_119])
#### [巡视公告](link_119)

巡视公告 2026-09-11[![Image 13](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/large/2026/09/24215102_60198.png)](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/dTyNjhE3PlsBtFlRnL57wA [link_120])
#### [报告！请查收南科学子的暑期社会实践答卷](link_120)

为引导同学们在实践中深学细悟习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想，深入学习领会党的二十大和二十届历次全会精神，南方科技大学团委开展2026年暑期“三下乡”社会实践活动暨“百千万工程”突击队行动，引领南科青年在“行走的思政课”中感受中国

# [南科聚焦 News ![Image 6](https://www.sustech.edu.cn/static/newest2-v4/img/icon/News.png)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/ [link_13])[南科大新闻网![Image 7](https://www.sustech.edu.cn/static/newest2-v4/img/jiantou/6.png)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/ [link_13])

![Image 8](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/full/2026/10/011790822150772209.jpg)### [南方科技大学举行升旗仪式 庆祝中华人民共和国成立77周年](link_115)

![Image 9](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/full/2026/08/221787368555120419.png)### [Nature | 南科大徐俊课题组合作揭示GPCR通过二聚/寡聚化重塑细胞信号通路改善药理活性的分子基础](link_116)

*   [![Image 10](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/large/2026/09/171789637358501217.jpg)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/html/202609/47893.html [link_117])
#### [南方科技大学以正确政绩观凝心铸魂 以实干担当推动高质量发展](link_117)

中央部署开展树立和践行正确政绩观学习教育以来，南方科技大学党委坚持以习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想为指导，深入学习贯彻习近平总书记重要讲话和重要指示批示精神，认真贯彻中央和省委、市委、市委教育工委相关工作要求，紧扣“立党为公、为民造福、科学决策、真抓实干”总要求，把学习教育作为全年工作的重中之重，一体推进学习研讨、查摆问题、整改整治、建章立制、开门教育，以学促干、以干践行，坚持通过锤炼党性确保党员干部树立和践行正确政绩观，在学思践悟中筑牢思想根基，在实干担当中践行初心使命。 2026-09-17[![Image 11](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/large/2026/09/201789888983895632.png)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/html/202609/47904.html [link_118])
#### [南方科技大学“鹏城南科一号”卫星成功入轨 “硬核”创新再结硕果](link_118)

9月20日12时03分，南方科技大学“鹏城南科一号（PEGA－SUS 1）” 暨鹏城首发卫星，由我国商业运载火箭力箭一号遥十八在酒泉卫星发射基地成功发射，顺利进入预定轨道。中国科学院院士、南方科技大学校长薛其坤与师生代表共同观礼卫星发射。 2026-09-20[![Image 12](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/large/2026/09/11102509_91181.png)](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/html/202609/47875.html [link_119])
#### [巡视公告](link_119)

巡视公告 2026-09-11[![Image 13](https://newshub.sustech.edu.cn/uploads/large/2026/09/24215102_60198.png)](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/dTyNjhE3PlsBtFlRnL57wA [link_120])
#### [报告！请查收南科学子的暑期社会实践答卷](link_120)

为引导同学们在实践中深学细悟习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想，深入学习领会党的二十大和二十届历次全会精神，南方科技大学团委开展2026年暑期“三下乡”社会实践活动暨“百千万工程”突击队行动，引领南科青年在“行走的思政课”中感受中国

# Board of Trustees

## Breadcrumb

*   [Home](https://www.kean.edu/)
*   [About](https://www.kean.edu/about)

## Overview

The Kean University Board of Trustees is the governing body of the University. It currently consists of 15 members appointed by the Governor of New Jersey, as well as a student trustee representative elected by the student body. Pursuant to the Higher Education Restructuring Act of 1994, the Board has general supervision and oversight of the University.

**The Higher Education Restructuring Act of 1994 empowers the Board to:**

*   Set tuition and fees and hold public hearings.
*   Recommend appointment of Trustees to Governor with Senate’s consent.
*   Determine the size and make up of Board of Trustees (7-15).
*   Invest monies, with other than Division of Investments, with approval of treasury.
*   Choose legal counsel.
*   Submit annual budget to Treasury.
*   Determine disputes for classified employees.
*   Conduct hearings on appeals under higher education law.
*   Approve facilities construction.
*   Approve programs within mission.
*   Create a public annual financial statement on government relations, public relations and legal costs.
*   Submit annual report on institutional condition.
*   Submit annual independent audit and management letter.
*   Adopt and use a corporate seal.
*   Determine policies for the organization, administration and development of the University.
*   Direct and control expenditures and transfers of funds appropriated to the University.
*   Appoint and fix the compensation of the President of the University, the executive officer of the University.
*   Upon the nomination of the President, appoint and fix the compensation of professional members of the academic, administrative and teaching staff.
*   Upon the nomination of the President, appoint, remove, promote and transfer such officers, agents, employees as may be required.
*   Grant diplomas, certificates and degrees.
*   Borrow money for the needs of the University.

Trustee appointments are for six years. Each board member serves until his or her successor is appointed. Each year a student trustee and student-alternate trustee is elected by the student body. Board members serve without compensation but are entitled to be reimbursed for all reasonable and necessary expenses.

**Current board officers are:**Chair of the Board Steve Fastook and Vice Chair of the Board Linda Lewis and Secretary of the Board Dr. Thomas Bistocchi.

# Kean Ocean

Find out more about our degree completion and graduate programs in Toms River and continue your educational journey through our unique partnership with Ocean County College.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bz0aEeGVkKI)

## About Kean Ocean

Kean Ocean is located on the Ocean County College campus in Toms River offering undergraduate transfer students and graduate students access to affordable [degree options](https://www.kean.edu/ocean/undergraduate-graduate-curriculum-sheets).

![Image 2: kean ocean student smiling](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2018-08/img_0747.jpg?itok=aEuWq2ZZ)

Kean Ocean offers:

*   **Academic**programs identical to those at Kean’s main campus
*   Courses taught by **Kean faculty members**in **small classes**at Kean Ocean’s state-of-the-art Gateway Building
*   Opportunities to **study abroad** at Wenzhou-Kean University in China or in 30 other nations
*   The **convenience** of studying close to home
*   **Among the lowest tuition and fees** in southern New Jersey

![Image 3: Transfer Honor Roll](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2023-07/Kean%20Transfer%20Honor%20Roll%20Badge.png?itok=Hy97XCaw)

Just starting your college career? You may be interested in the **[OCC/Kean Ocean combined degree program.](https://www.ocean.edu/)**It’s **one of the most affordable and convenient ways to obtain a 4-year degree**on a single campus in New Jersey. Students completing their associate’s degree can seamlessly continue on with their study for a Kean bachelor’s degree with Kean courses offered on the OCC campus.

![Image 4: Kean Military Friendly 25-25 Gold](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/quarter_width/public/2025-09/MFS25%E2%80%9326_1-1200x1200-1.png?itok=zBOWnNlp)

Veteran Student Services provides transition services to veterans, service members, and dependents under the Kean Veterans Educational Transition Services Program,**Kean V.E.T.S**. We are dedicated to creating a seamless transition from soldier to student by providing a multitude of services at Kean and the surrounding community. Click on the Military Friendly logo to get started.

# Kean Ocean

Find out more about our degree completion and graduate programs in Toms River and continue your educational journey through our unique partnership with Ocean County College.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bz0aEeGVkKI)

## About Kean Ocean

Kean Ocean is located on the Ocean County College campus in Toms River offering undergraduate transfer students and graduate students access to affordable [degree options](https://www.kean.edu/ocean/undergraduate-graduate-curriculum-sheets).

![Image 2: kean ocean student smiling](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2018-08/img_0747.jpg?itok=aEuWq2ZZ)

Kean Ocean offers:

*   **Academic**programs identical to those at Kean’s main campus
*   Courses taught by **Kean faculty members**in **small classes**at Kean Ocean’s state-of-the-art Gateway Building
*   Opportunities to **study abroad** at Wenzhou-Kean University in China or in 30 other nations
*   The **convenience** of studying close to home
*   **Among the lowest tuition and fees** in southern New Jersey

![Image 3: Transfer Honor Roll](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2023-07/Kean%20Transfer%20Honor%20Roll%20Badge.png?itok=Hy97XCaw)

Just starting your college career? You may be interested in the **[OCC/Kean Ocean combined degree program.](https://www.ocean.edu/)**It’s **one of the most affordable and convenient ways to obtain a 4-year degree**on a single campus in New Jersey. Students completing their associate’s degree can seamlessly continue on with their study for a Kean bachelor’s degree with Kean courses offered on the OCC campus.

![Image 4: Kean Military Friendly 25-25 Gold](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/quarter_width/public/2025-09/MFS25%E2%80%9326_1-1200x1200-1.png?itok=zBOWnNlp)

Veteran Student Services provides transition services to veterans, service members, and dependents under the Kean Veterans Educational Transition Services Program,**Kean V.E.T.S**. We are dedicated to creating a seamless transition from soldier to student by providing a multitude of services at Kean and the surrounding community. Click on the Military Friendly logo to get started.

[![Image 6: Kean University alumnus Trevor Signorino, Class of 2019](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/highlight/public/2019-05/kid-step%20and%20repeat.jpg?h=9bdb28a7&itok=IfvaDFfL) A ‘Model’ Kean Graduate](https://www.kean.edu/news/model-kean-graduate)

# Wenzhou-Kean University Approved to Offer Graduate Programs

Nov 12, 2019

![Image 2: An overhead shot of the Wenzhou-Kean University campus](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2019-11/WKU%202019.png?itok=Ad6nCJbT)

The Ministry of Education of China recently granted Wenzhou-Kean University approval to launch 11 graduate-level programs, marking a pivotal moment in the growth of Kean’s campus in China.

The eight master’s and three doctoral programs are in computer science, education, business and accounting, science, psychology and counseling, and architecture.

"We will offer qualitatively superior programs, hire the best-qualified faculty, and continue to cooperate in the best interests of our students,” said Kean University President Dawood Farahi, Ph.D. “This is an amazing start to the second phase of the development of Wenzhou-Kean University as a global world-class university in China."

Admission requirements for the WKU graduate programs will be consistent with those of Kean USA. WKU’s goal is to begin rolling out some programs for Fall 2020.

The Wenzhou municipal government has provided an additional 20 million renminbi (RMB) for each of the next five years to recruit internationally for outstanding faculty with strong backgrounds in research.

“I am thrilled that WKU has been approved to offer a wide range of graduate programs,” said Kean’s Provost and Vice President for Research and Faculty Jeffrey H. Toney, Ph.D. “Our graduate programs will prepare students to become successful professionals in the global marketplace.”

More than 2,400 undergraduate students are currently enrolled at WKU with thousands more expected in the coming years.

The 11 graduate programs are:

*   Accounting (M.S.)

*   Architecture (M.Arch.)

*   Biotechnology Science (M.S.)

*   Computer Information Systems (M.S.)

*   Educational Administration (M.A.)

*   Global Business (MBA)

*   Instruction and Curriculum (M.A.)

*   Psychology (M.A.)

*   Combined School and Clinical Psychology (Psy.D.)

*   Counseling and Supervision (Ph.D.)

*   Educational Leadership (Ed.D.)

"This speaks to the academic excellence and scholarship that WKU has been pursuing for the past seven years,” said Eric Yixin Yang, Ph.D., Kean’s associate provost for academic affairs and acting vice chancellor for Wenzhou-Kean University. “The graduate programs will provide Chinese and international students with a unique graduate education that provides the vigorous and innovative Kean curriculum within a Chinese modern, economic and cultural context.”

WKU is located in the foothills of Wenzhou, China, a city with 9 million people. Each year, a majority of its graduates go on to pursue post-baccalaureate degrees, some to the most prestigious universities in the world.

"By offering graduate programs at Wenzhou-Kean University, we are giving our students the opportunity to continue their education at WKU," said Christine Thorpe, Ed.D., dean of Kean's Nathan Weiss Graduate College. "These are high-demand programs that will educate tomorrow's leaders."

# More than 200 Receive Degrees at Wenzhou-Kean Commencement

Jun 04, 2017

![Image 2](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/f424a72fcbbca838234997eed2f031a9.jpg?itok=e-dHIjxF)

Wenzhou-Kean University (WKU) in Wenzhou, China held its second commencement on Saturday, June 3, conferring bachelor’s degrees on 213 graduates at the Wenzhou Grand Theater. Faculty, administrators, family and friends joined the graduates in the majestic theater for a ceremony filled with pomp, circumstance, music and dance. A partnership between Kean University and Wenzhou University in Wenzhou, China, WKU is the only public American university in China.

Kean President Dawood Farahi, Ph.D., told the graduates that their commencement is special for the United States and China.

“It shows what can be accomplished when we work together toward the same goal of developing world-class, global citizens,” Farahi said. “Today, you are living proof that there are no borders in higher education—in fact, your accomplishment proves that higher education is a great international equalizer.”

With its second graduating class, WKU continues to assert itself as a leader in global education, with nearly 70 percent of the Class of 2017 pursuing graduate degrees in the fall, and nearly half of them heading overseas for their studies – at Kean University in Union, New Jersey and other prestigious institutions such as Brown University, Johns Hopkins University, University of Pennsylvania, Columbia University, London School of Economics and Political Science and Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Nearly a third of the graduates have been hired at some of the top companies in China, including the Bank of China, Bank of Ningbo, Agricultural Bank of China, Faurecia Group, and GrantThornton LLP.

Economist Lin Jianhai, Ph.D., secretary general of the International Monetary Fund, peppered his Keynote Address with personal stories to highlight the four principles he has followed in his career and his life – be positive; work hard and work smart; keep learning; and grow with the world.

“You are born and are growing in a dynamic inter-connected new century,” Lin said. “You are destined to face different challenges than your parents, but you are also equipped with better and sharper tools. A fulfilling, distinctive life is an achievement, not something that will fall into your life because you are a nice person. Don’t wait for inspiration or passion to find you. Go out and find it yourself and grab it with both hands. It is called commencement because you will continue on your adventure from this point.”

The commencement ceremony featured stirring renditions of the United States and China national anthems, a traditional Chinese music performance, as well as performances from student choral and dance groups.

Consul General of the United States Consulate General in Shanghai Hanscom Smith told the graduates that they have thrived in an environment that “encourages dialogue, exploration, and cooperation.”

"I can’t help but wonder what the world will look like when it is time for Wenzhou-Kean’s commencement many years in the future," said Smith. "I like to imagine an even more open, more cooperative and more peaceful world. One that institutions like Wenzhou-Kean are actively working to promote and one that many of you seated here today will start building as soon as you leave this room."

Wenzhou-Kean University, located on a 500-acre campus in the foothills of Wenzhou in Zhejiang Province, welcomed its first cohort of students in 2012 and graduated its inaugural class in 2016. WKU offers an American university education to Chinese, international and visiting Kean USA students. All classes are taught exclusively in English.

Professor Lu Shanzhen, chancellor of Wenzhou-Kean University, told the graduates that ceaseless study, a focus on innovation and a grateful heart will guide them in shaping their futures and changing the world.

“From the moment you chose Wenzhou-Kean University, your life began to change,” Lu said. “The university brings the Chinese and Western cultures together, and offers an education featuring critical thinking and innovation. All these have enabled you to better understand each other, to better see the true world, and to be a better you.”

In addressing her classmates, valedictorian Pan Lijun noted that WKU taught her to focus on building skills for professional and personal success.

“This school gave me problem solving skills. I believe this is the advantage of the WKU-style education,” Pan said. “Being thrown out of my comfort zone was an excellent and valuable experience, not only because I was forced to learn new things and get great teamwork experience, but because those constant challenges make you feel invincible. The diversity and challenges in this university were truly gifts to me.”

Wenzhou-Kean University was borne out of a 2006 “sister city” meeting between Dr. Farahi and the People’s Republic of China President Xi Jinping, who was governor of Zhejiang Province at the time. Together, they developed a plan to create an American-style university in Wenzhou for Chinese and international students seeking a western education, while offering Kean USA students an opportunity to gain a global perspective through study abroad in China at no additional cost.

Kean University Trustee Lamont Repollet, Ph.D., praised the graduates for embracing the “idea” of WKU, calling them “trailblazers and pioneers.”

“You took a risk when you chose Wenzhou-Kean. I first visited Wenzhou in October 2012, and when I arrived, there were no academic buildings, no residence halls, no canteens and no libraries. You took a chance on Wenzhou-Kean University, and your investment paid off,” Repollet said.

Nearly 1,600 undergraduate students attend Wenzhou-Kean University, and enrollment is projected to be 3,500 by 2020. WKU offers academic programs in the natural and physical sciences, computer science, business, English and graphic design on a campus that continues to expand. A new Global Business School academic building is expected to open in fall 2017, and new buildings for Michael Graves College and a student learning and activity center are scheduled to open in early 2019. In addition, gardens and landscaping are being added in an ongoing beautification project that is part of the University’s master plan.

# Center for International Studies

At Kean, we believe in providing a world-class education to our students. That means offering opportunities to see the world and learn from different perspectives, so that you're prepared to compete in the global marketplace after graduation.

Kean students study abroad in many countries, including at our English-speaking campus in Wenzhou, China. We also welcome students and scholars from around the world at our campuses in New Jersey.

![Image 2: MGC Travellearn](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2024-02/MGC_Travellearn.png?itok=PbkxFyHE)

![Image 3: Kean students in a gorgeous outdoor setting in Northern Ireland 2023](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_4x3/public/2023-07/Ireland_Travelearn_310.jpg?h=71976bb4&itok=8R0YmNqY)

## Travelearns (Short-Term Study Abroad Programs)

Travelearns are short term, faculty led study abroad programs. These allow students to continue working toward their degree while completing a short-term study abroad program for 7-10 days .

Travelearns tend to focus on a specific topic and may include lectures, internships, research and excursions. Travelearns at Kean University primarily travel abroad, but occasionally occur domestically.

[More Information](https://www.kean.edu/offices/international-education/travelearn)

[Student Information](https://www.kean.edu/offices/international-education/travelearn/travelearn-information-students)

[Faculty information](https://www.kean.edu/offices/international-education/travelearn/international-education-faculty)

![Image 4: Kean students in Costa Rica](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_4x3/public/2024-02/Copy%20of%2020230310_061912%280%29.jpg?h=28dd254b&itok=rR_MbhhI)

### **Summer 2026**

![Image 5: Wenzhou Kean University](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_4x3/public/2022-11/WKU_Students%20on%20Grass.jpg?h=f2fcf546&itok=p66RLZ-3)

## WKU Exchange

Kean University is the only American public university to offer a full campus in China. Students from Kean USA and institutions across the country can study in the fully English-speaking environment alongside students from across China.

[WKU information](https://www.kean.edu/wku)

[Apply for WKU Exchange](https://keanabroad.via-trm.com/program_brochure/11727/term-information)

As the only public American university with a full campus in China, we are uniquely poised to deliver on that promise. You can study at Wenzhou-Kean University for the same price as studying at one of our campuses in the United States.

**Learn more about this unique opportunity and spend a semester in China!**

## Study Abroad

Study abroad takes place outside of the country in which you are enrolled as a student. It may include participating in courses, internships, research, service learning, and other learning activities.

Students at Kean University have three main options for studying abroad: our[WKU Exchange](https://www.kean.edu/wku), one of our many Spring or Summer[Travelearns](https://www.kean.edu/offices/international-education/travelearn), or participating in a [program provider trip](https://www.kean.edu/offices/international-education/study-abroad-program-provider). Students can choose the experience that best suits their interests, ranging from studying abroad for a full academic year, semester, or 7-10 days.

## International Student Services

The Center for International Studies takes pride in welcoming a diverse group of students and scholars from around the world to Kean U.S.A. each year. We stand ready to help with immigration and visa regulations and other support to help ensure you have a positive and meaningful experience.

Kean University takes pride in welcoming international students from all over the globe who are pursuing their studies.

In order to get more information on the office processes, please visit our[International Students and Scholars page](https://www.kean.edu/offices/international-education/international-students-scholars).

You can also visit our[FAQ page](https://www.kean.edu/offices/international-education/international-faqs)to have further questions answered.

If you have immediate questions that are not answered on our website, please contact our Center for International Studies at cis@kean.edu .

## Study Abroad With A Program Provider

Kean offers Study Abroad programs of longer duration, including a Winter term, Summer term, Semester, or an Academic year, by partnering with outside companies (program providers).

This type of study abroad program is more "flexible" as it allows students to select their location and duration of study.

[Program Provider Information](https://www.kean.edu/offices/international-education/study-abroad-program-provider)

[Apply now](https://keanabroad.via-trm.com/visitor-programs-v2)

## Update for International Students: New DHS Regulations

On July 17, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) published new federal regulations affecting international students studying in the United States. The Center for International Studies (CIS) is actively reviewing the regulations and working to understand their impact on Kean students.

**Important**: This page provides a summary of the new DHS regulations. Guidance may change as additional information becomes available. The Center for International Studies will update this page as new guidance is released.

For more information, please review the [**U.S. government FAQs**](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/final-rule-establishing-a-fixed-time-period-of-admission-and-an-extension-of-stay-procedure-faq) about the new regulations.

### **What You Need to Know**

*   **Effective September 15, 2026**

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security is replacing Duration of Status (D/S) with fixed four-year maximum admissions for F and J nonimmigrants. Students who need additional time to complete their programs must file an Extension of Stay (EOS) application directly with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).

*   **Fixed End Dates**

Your stay will be limited to your program end date or four years, whichever is shorter. If you need more time to complete your program, you must apply to USCIS for an Extension of Stay before your current end date.

*   **Grace Period**

The post-completion grace period has been reduced from to 30 days (down from 60 days).

*   **Transfer and Program Restrictions**

New limits restrict your ability to transfer schools or change majors during your first year.

*   **Current D/S Holders**

If you are already in the United States before September 15, 2026, you will generally retain your D/S for up to four years, provided you maintain your status and do not travel outside the United States or require an extension.

### **Additional Information**

For more information, please review the [**U.S. government FAQs**](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/final-rule-establishing-a-fixed-time-period-of-admission-and-an-extension-of-stay-procedure-faq) about the new regulations.

### **Contact the Center for International Studies**

The Center for International Studies remains committed to supporting all Kean international students throughout this process and will continue to share updates as additional guidance becomes available. We ask our international students to please check their Kean email regularly for the latest information.

If you have specific questions about how this new rule will impact you, please contact us here:

*   **Email:**[cis@kean.edu](mailto:cis@kean.edu)
*   **Kean Union & Ocean:** (908) 737-0350
*   **Kean Jersey City:** (201) 200-3561

## 南科大简介

南方科技大学（简称：南科大）是深圳在中国高等教育改革发展的时代背景下创建的一所高起点、高定位的公办新型研究型大学。2022年2月14日，教育部等三部委公布第二轮“双一流”建设高校及建设学科名单，南方科技大学及数学学科入选“双一流”建设高校及建设学科名单。学校借鉴世界一流理工科大学的学科设置和办学模式，以理工医为主，兼具商科和特色人文，以及交叉学科协同发展的一流学科体系，在本科、硕士、博士层次办学，在一系列新的学科方向上开展研究，使学校成为引领社会发展的思想库和新知识、新技术的源泉。

南方科技大学扎根中国大地，紧抓粤港澳大湾区、深圳先行示范区“双区”驱动，深圳经济特区、深圳先行示范区“双区”叠加的历史机遇，发扬“敢闯敢试、求真务实、改革创新、追求卓越”的创校精神，突出“创知、创新、创业”的办学特色，践行“明德求是、日新自强”的校训精神，努力服务创新型国家建设及深圳国际化现代化创新型城市建设，快速建设成为聚集一流师资、培养拔尖创新人才、创造国际一流学术成果并推动科技应用的国际化高水平研究型大学，为尽早实现建成世界一流研究型大学的宏伟目标打下坚实基础。

## 李凤亮

**党委书记**[_个人主页_](https://www.sustech.edu.cn/zh/gyr.html)

南方科技大学已经踏上第二个十年征程，我们不断加强党的建设，扎根湾区、服务国家、放眼全球，发扬担当精神、创新精神、卓越精神、探索精神，加快将南科大建成扎根中国大地、具有全球重要影响力的新型研究型大学，力争成为我国新时代高水平科技自立自强进程中新型研究型大学的冲锋舟和先遣队，争创中国特色社会主义大学范例。

## 薛其坤

**校长**[_个人主页_](https://www.sustech.edu.cn/zh/csy.html)

我们努力为探索新型研究型大学发展路径提供“南科大经验”，凝练总结拔尖创新人才培养的“南科大模式”，打造一个服务经济社会发展的“南科大样本”，走出一条高等教育改革创新的“南科大路径”，以卓越思维、使命思维、非常思维、辩证思维统筹发展规划，推动南科大成为有理想、敢担当、勇改革、有理性的受人尊重的大学。

## 师资力量

截至目前，南方科技大学已签约引进教师约1300人，包括院士52人，国际会士70人，青年科学基金项目（A类）获得者59人、青年科学基金项目（B类）获得者49人。教学科研系列教师90%以上具有海外工作经验，60%以上具有在世界排名前100名大学工作或学习的经历，高层次人才占教研系列50%以上。

学校着力建立有利于教育公平、创新人才选拔的多元录取机制和先进的全面教育体系。学校率先改革招生制度，采用“基于高考的综合评价录取模式”招收优秀学生。学校以“学分制、书院制、导师制”和“国际化、个性化、多元化”为核心和特色，大力培养拔尖创新人才。学校采用书院制管理，目前共设立致仁、树仁、致诚、树德、致新、树礼、创业7个书院。

## A Message from President Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D. - Friday, October 2, 2026

Dear Kean Community,  
  
This week, Kean’s commitment to social mobility was on display at Harwood Arena, where our Fall Career, Internship and Part-Time Job Fair connected students and alumni with more than 115 employers and a wide range of potential employment opportunities. A conversation with an employer can open the door to an internship, introduce a career path, or begin a lasting professional relationship. For a student building a network for the first time, that access matters. Our responsibility is to help students gain the knowledge and connections they need to pursue the opportunities that their education creates.  
  
That is social mobility in action. Education should help people improve their economic circumstances and expand their ability to build stronger futures for themselves and their families. A meaningful career can support a stable home and give a parent greater capacity to invest in a child’s future. This week’s job fair made that connection tangible.  
  
On the same day, I participated in the Governor’s Conference on Housing and Economic Development, hosted by the New Jersey Redevelopment Authority, where our discussion examined the role of anchor institutions in strengthening communities. During the conference, I discussed the connections our students were making at Harwood Arena as a clear example of an anchor institution’s responsibility to connect a university’s resources with the aspirations of the people it serves.  
  
Anchor institutions have deep, lasting ties to their communities. Universities, hospitals and faith-based organizations often fill that role because their missions and resources connect them to communities across generations. For Kean, being an anchor institution means accepting responsibility for how our work expands opportunity and contributes to the well-being of our neighbors.  
  
Housing is an important part of that equation. A student needs a secure place to live and study. A working parent needs stability to pursue a degree or new skills. A career with opportunities for advancement can help sustain that foundation. Real progress requires education, employment and housing partners to work together around the needs of residents.  
  
That same theme carries into the Season Two premiere of _Climb Higher with Her_, hosted by my wife, Kean University First Lady Darlene Repollet. Darlene opens the season with entrepreneur and affordable housing developer Adenah Bayoh, founder and CEO of Foya Development Group. In the episode, Adenah shares how her ventures create wealth and opportunity in underserved communities. Her work offers students a powerful example of how entrepreneurship can support individual success and community well-being.  
  
As an anchor institution, Kean also has a responsibility to make the experience and insight of leaders accessible to others. Through _Climb Higher with Her_, Darlene brings leadership lessons and career perspectives to our students, alumni and wider community. The podcast complements Career Services’ work by helping listeners understand how professionals build careers, navigate challenges and create opportunities for others. Together, these resources can help students see new possibilities for themselves and take informed steps toward their goals.  
  
These efforts strengthen the broader economy, too. Employers need talented people who can solve problems and adapt as industries change. Students need opportunities to apply their learning and develop professionally. When graduates secure meaningful work, support local businesses or become entrepreneurs themselves, the benefits of their education extend throughout the community. Workforce development and social mobility advance together when more people can participate in the prosperity they help create.  
  
From our longstanding presence in Union to our metropolitan campus in Jersey City, Kean must continue strengthening connections with residents and community partners. Our public impact grows when educational opportunities lead to greater economic security and stronger communities. That requires listening, sustained relationships and follow-through long after an event ends.  
  
I thank our Office of Career Services, participating employers and everyone who supported this week’s job fair. Students and alumni, follow up on the connections you made and continue using Career Services as you pursue your next step. I also invite our entire community to listen to Darlene’s conversation with Adenah Bayoh on [_Climb Higher with Her_](https://www.kean.edu/climb-higher-her), available on Spotify and Apple Podcasts, and consider how its lessons can inform your own journey.  
  
As Kean continues to Rise and Climb Higher, we must keep creating pathways for others to do the same. [](https://www.kean.edu/presidential-announcements)  
  
Sincerely,  
  
Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D.  
President

## A Message from President Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D. - Friday, September 25, 2026

Dear Kean Community,  
  
At Kean University, we often talk about public impact. But what does that really mean?  
  
For me, public impact is about what happens when the knowledge, talent, research and resources of a university move beyond our campuses and improve people’s lives. It means asking what difference do we make? What problems do we help solve? What opportunities do we create? And whose lives are better because Kean University is here?  
  
This week offered a powerful reminder of why those questions matter as Kean continues to rise and Climb Higher. Kean rose to No. 68 among national universities in the latest _U.S. News & World Report_ Best Colleges rankings for social mobility, up 13 spots from last year. The recognition reflects something at the heart of our mission: creating opportunities that can change the trajectory of students, families and communities.  
  
We also saw that mission in action this week at Kean Jersey City as we welcomed members of the freshman class at convocation. The gathering was another reminder that wherever our students begin their Kean journey, our responsibility is to give them the opportunity and support to climb higher.

![Image 3: Kean Jersey City freshman convocation](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2026-09/Freshman_convocation.jpg?itok=U_sB_WKN)

Our students demonstrate every day what happens when access meets opportunity. Their success is helping Kean emerge nationally as an institution where social mobility is not an abstract idea. It is a lived experience. Students come through our doors, discover their potential and earn their degrees. As they rise, their families and communities rise with them.  
  
The next evolution of that work is extending public impact into global impact. Our work in Ireland this week reflects that broader reach.Alumna Christina Carey Dunleavy ’98, a Kean University Foundation board member and generous donor, helped us cultivate a relationship with University College Dublin, where she earned her master’s degree in business. Through that connection, we are exploring ways to deepen academic collaboration and create new opportunities for faculty and students.

![Image 4: Kean delegation visits Ireland. ](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2026-09/Ireland.png?itok=Qfq_HQZJ)

One area is educational leadership. Through our College of Education, we are evaluating opportunities to bring educational leaders from different countries together to study leadership, innovation and the challenges confronting educational systems around the world. Tomorrow’s leaders must be able to operate across cultures and borders while understanding how technology, artificial intelligence and rapidly changing economies are transforming education.  
  
We are also exploring an exciting opportunity around architecture, design-build and the built environment. Kean students and faculty have already taken part in international experiences in Brazil and China that demonstrate how architecture can become an instrument of public impact. By working directly with communities, students can identify real problems and use design to develop solutions that make places more responsive to the needs of the people who live there.  
  
Ireland offers another opportunity to extend that model. Imagine Irish, American and Chinese architecture students collaborating on challenges. Imagine a graduate student from Ireland studying at Kean in New Jersey, using the New York metropolitan region as a living laboratory and then having the opportunity to study at Wenzhou-Kean University in China.  
  
That kind of collaboration would bring together students from three countries, each with different experiences and perspectives, to learn from one another and tackle shared challenges. That is global learning. And when that learning is used to solve real problems, it becomes global impact. That is the future I see for Kean. We should not measure our international success simply by the number of countries we visit or agreements we sign. We should measure it by the opportunities and solutions that those relationships produce. And wherever Kean goes, our purpose should remain the same: listen, learn, collaborate and leave something better than we found it. That is how an urban research university fulfills its public mission. [](https://www.kean.edu/presidential-announcements)  
  
And that is how Kean University will continue to Rise and Climb Higher, from social mobility to public impact and from public impact to global impact. Together, we rise. Together, we climb. And together, we make an impact.

Sincerely,

Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D.  
President  
Kean University

## A Message from President Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D. - Friday, September 18, 2026

Dear Kean Community,  
  
There is something reassuring about this stage of the semester. The excitement of Opening Day is beginning to settle into the steady rhythm of university life. Class schedules become familiar, conversations continue beyond the classroom and faces we passed just a few weeks ago become people we greet by name. Across our campuses, we are finding our footing and building the routines that help us move forward with confidence.  
  
For our students, that rhythm takes shape in many ways: discovering a favorite place to study, preparing for the next assignment, connecting with a professor, or balancing coursework with a job and responsibilities at home. Our first-year and transfer students are becoming more familiar with academic buildings and the paths between classes. What once required a map is gradually becoming part of the day. As you find your way, I want you to know that you belong here, and we are committed to your success.  
  
To our newest students, give yourselves room to adjust. Confidence grows through experience, and asking for help is part of that growth. You do not need to wait until you are struggling to seek guidance. Introduce yourself, visit office hours, ask questions, explore a student organization and make use of the people and resources here to support you. You bring experiences and perspectives that strengthen Kean, and we want you to feel connected to this community.  
  
Our faculty and staff are also establishing their rhythm. Evolving responsibilities and the continued integration of our campuses require flexibility and thoughtful coordination. Behind every class, student service and welcoming campus space are people balancing their commitment to Kean with their own families and personal responsibilities. I recognize that effort, and I am grateful for it. The care you extend to our students must also shape how we treat and support one another.  
  
Wellness must have a place in the routines we build. I encourage our teams to communicate clearly, establish realistic priorities and respect the time people need to recharge. A strong university depends on people who feel supported in both their work and their lives. For our students, that means making room for rest and connection alongside academic responsibilities.  
  
Our Welcome Back Walk on Tuesday, September 22, from 8 to 9 a.m. across campuses gives us a chance to put that commitment into practice. I invite all of you to join in. Bring a classmate or colleague and spend some time together outside. I encourage you all to step away from your usual schedules and get to know the people who share our campuses.  
  
Congratulations to the Kean Jersey City women’s soccer team on winning its home opener against Bucks County Community College. Thank you to Vice President of Athletics and Recreation Kelly Williams for performing the honorary coin flip before the game. Let’s continue to support our student-athletes throughout the season.

Kean Jersey City will celebrate another milestone next Thursday, September 24, with Freshman Convocation. To our first-year students on the Jersey City campus, I encourage you to join your classmates for this occasion and take pride in the work that brought you here. You are an important part of our Kean community, and I look forward to what you will contribute and accomplish in the years ahead.  
  
The unified Kean system continues to take shape, and our daily interactions help turn institutional connections into a shared sense of community. As we settle into this semester, I ask each of you to remain attentive to those who are still finding their way. Extend an invitation and make room for connection. The rhythm we create together should help every member of our community feel that they have a place in Kean’s future.[](https://www.kean.edu/presidential-announcements)  
  
Together, we will continue to Climb Higher.  
  
Sincerely,

Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D.

## A Message from President Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D. - Friday, September 11, 2026

Dear Kean Community,  
  
This week, across all of Kean’s campuses, our students entered their second week of classes and continued finding their place within our University community. Although each of our locations has its own character and strengths, the experiences we shared this week reminded us that we are connected by one mission, one community and one unified Kean system.  
  
On Tuesday, we raised the Kean flag at Kean Jersey City to mark this historic new chapter. As the flag rose above our metropolitan campus, it carried a powerful message: every student, faculty member, staff member and alumnus, regardless of location, is part of one Kean. The flag is more than a symbol. It represents our shared identity, our commitment to educational opportunity and our belief that the future of Kean will be shaped by the collective strength of our entire University system.  
  
That same spirit of connection was reflected in our celebration of Kean Day, one of our most meaningful campus traditions. Across our locations, students were introduced to the clubs, programs and organizations that make Kean such a vibrant place to learn and grow. Kean Day reminds students that their university experience extends far beyond the classroom. It is found in the relationships they build, the organizations they join, the interests they discover and the opportunities they embrace. These connections create a sense of belonging that can shape a student’s years at Kean, as well as the direction of their life.  
  
I invite you all to bring that Kean spirit to Alumni Stadium tomorrow at 1 p.m. as the Kean football team takes on Maritime College. Let's fill the stands, support our student-athletes and celebrate the pride that unites us as one Kean community.  
  
This week we also paused to remember the victims of the September 11 attacks. Twenty-five years later, we continue to honor the lives that were lost, the families forever changed and the first responders and ordinary citizens whose courage revealed the very best of humanity during one of our nation’s darkest moments. For our Kean community, located in the heart of New Jersey and the greater New York metropolitan region, this remembrance remains deeply personal.  
  
Belonging and remembrance may appear to represent different experiences, but both ask something important of us. They ask us to recognize our connection to one another, to honor the communities we inherit and to accept responsibility for the communities we are building. That responsibility is especially meaningful at a university, where each new academic year brings together people with different backgrounds and aspirations around a shared belief in the transformative power of education.  
  
As we move forward, let us carry the meaning of this week with us. Let us welcome every student into the life of the University, honor those whose lives and sacrifices shaped our history and continue building a unified Kean system in which every member of our community knows they belong and understands that they have a role in our shared future.[](https://www.kean.edu/presidential-announcements)  
  
Sincerely,

Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D.   
President

# Wenzhou-Kean University Celebrates 10th Anniversary

Nov 30, 2021

![Image 2: Wenzhou-Kean University's architecture building, with blue sky and Wenzhou-Kean in large letters on the lawn.](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/mobile_width/public/2021-11/Wenzhou-Architecture-Building-615.jpg?itok=DLJ8_h3L)

Wenzhou-Kean University, which brings American-style higher education to China and builds cultural and educational bridges between the two countries, celebrated its 10th anniversary this month with events in China and at Kean USA.

“The best way for us to honor this moment is to look at where we are and reflect on where we started,” said Kean President Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D. “The partnership between WKU and Kean USA creates a path for students on each campus to engage in valuable, global, cross-cultural exchange, which allows students to share diverse backgrounds and gain experiences that reach far beyond the classroom.”

![Image 3: Flags of the US and China](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/half_width/public/2021-11/Untitled-12.jpg?itok=oqXT3pJo)

Built on a 500-acre campus in mountainous Zhejiang Province, Wenzhou-Kean University – or WKU – has grown to serve 3,500 students pursuing degrees in architecture, design, computer science, business and public management and more.

The anniversary celebration in Wenzhou included a traditional art and calligraphy exhibition, musical performances, a cultural festival, academic forums and more.

At Hynes Hall on Kean’s Union campus, President Repollet and members of his executive team joined elected officials, faculty, staff and students to also mark the anniversary.

“To all who have played a role in creating, supporting and studying at WKU, I say, ‘Congratulations on a milestone anniversary,’” Repollet said. “The incredible progress made at Wenzhou-Kean University over the last 10 years is proof we can climb even higher than we imagine.”

Former Kean President Dawood Farahi, Ph.D., spoke on video about the complex process of making WKU a reality.

“We did something spectacular, and it needs to move on in the direction of world-class education with the resources needed to create one of the best universities of international stature in China,” he said. "I am sure we can do that."

The Kean event included a performance by two WKU students currently studying at the Union campus. Yiran Song and Zhuqing Pu sang a Chinese song, translated as _Kepler_, about two stars shining brightly together. The stars represent Kean and WKU, they said.

Song, a 20-year-old mathematics student from Chongqing, China, said his time at Kean has been a “wonderful experience.”

“I can feel the culture of the country and the school,” he said.

![Image 4: WKU 10th anniversary celebration](https://www.kean.edu/sites/default/files/styles/half_width/public/2021-11/Untitled-14.jpg?itok=myXafSZ5)

WKU's 10th anniversary celebration spanned the globe with events in Wenzhou, China and at Kean USA.

The agreement creating WKU struck by Kean and the Chinese government was one of the first of its kind. The campus, which continues to grow, resembles an American college. Kean administers academic programs, and all classes are taught in English.

It also offers Kean students a study abroad experience in China at the same cost as attending Kean USA. More than 1,000 WKU students have also studied at Kean USA.

During the pandemic, when world travel was curtailed, the two campuses offered virtual internships to students across the globe.

WKU Chancellor Wang Li called the past decade “an endeavor of shouldering significant responsibilities and missions” and pursuing innovation and excellence. As the world recovers from the pandemic, he said WKU provides an important connection.

"At this new crucial starting point, we should insist on our original intention of cultivating international talents and strive for facilitating cultural exchanges while raising WKU up to a higher-level university with its one-of-a-kind features,” he said.

Jessica Goldsmith Barzilay, executive director of International Studies & WKU Student Affairs, said studying at WKU is “one of the most extraordinary experiences” offered to Kean students. “It is a game changer as far as career prospects, but it is also a game changer as far as life perspective. Students report it was the greatest part of their college experience,” she said.

Jamaica Evelyn, a junior history/education major minoring in Chinese studies, said she changed her career plans after studying at WKU in 2019. She now wants to teach English abroad so she can travel to different countries.

“I had an amazing time at WKU. I have been waiting to go back ever since I arrived home,” she said. The Hillside resident said going to WKU was her first time traveling abroad.

“I made friends on campus and off campus. The campus was gorgeous and the weather was perfect,” she said. “Being able to meet people with similar interests and goals is a wonderful experience. With today’s technology, there is no such thing as a language barrier.”

The WKU campus includes new buildings for business and public management; the sciences; architecture, design and computing sciences; as well as dormitories, dining halls, and indoor and outdoor athletic facilities. Future plans include incorporating adaptive reuse of historic structures in an adjacent village, as well as a light rail system and links to high-speed trains and an international airport.

At the close of his remarks, Repollet toasted the visionary leaders and public servants who saw the potential of global partnership and the pioneering students, faculty and staff who took a chance on WKU.

“To our collective future, for surely it shines brighter each time our students engage in cross-cultural learning, friendship and mutual understanding,” he concluded.
